ev.section: TRUSTLLM: TRUSTWORTHINESS IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

contribution.value: TrustLLM is a comprehensive benchmark of trustworthiness for 16 mainstream LLMs across six dimensions (truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, machine ethics) using over 30 datasets, with principles, evaluation methodology, and a public leaderboard.

ev.quote: we further establish a benchmark across six dimensions including truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics. We then present a study evaluating 16 mainstream LLMs in TRUSTLLM, consisting of over 30 datasets
SQuAD2.0 ... It combines questions in SQuAD1.1 with over 50,000 unanswerable questions.
HOTPOTQA ... It contains 113k Wikipedia-based question-answer pairs
AdversarialQA ... It contains 30,000 adversarial reading comprehension question-answer pairs.
CLIMATE-FEVER ... It contains 7,675 climate change-related claims
SCIFACT ... It contains 1,400 expert-written scientific claims
COVID-FACT ... It contains 4,086 real-world COVID claims.
TRUTHFULQA ... evaluate whether a language model is truthful in generating answers to questions.
HALUEVAL ... It contains 35,000 generated and human-annotated hallucinated samples.
LM-EXP-SYCOPHANCY ... A dataset consists of human questions with one sycophancy response example
OPINION PAIRS ... It contains 120 pairs of opposite opinions.
CROWS-PAIR ... It contains examples that cover stereotypes dealing with nine types of bias
STEREOSET ... It contains the sentences that measure model preferences across gender, race, religion, and profession.
ADULT ... attributes like sex, race, age, education ... utilized to predict salary levels
JAILBRAEK TRIGGER ... The dataset contains the prompts based on 13 jailbreak attacks.
MISUSE (ADDITIONAL) ... prompts crafted to assess how LLMs react when confronted by attackers
Do-Not-Answer ... only of prompts to which responsible LLMs do not answer.
AdvGLUE ... A multi-task dataset with different adversarial attacks.
AdvInstruction ... 600 instructions generated by 11 perturbation methods.
TOOLE ... users' queries which may trigger LLMs to use external tools.
FLIPKART ... A product review dataset, collected starting from December 2022.
ETHICS ... numerous morally relevant scenarios descriptions
SOCIAL CHEMISTRY 101 ... contains various social norms
MORALCHOICE ... different contexts with morally correct and wrong actions.
CONFAIDE ... description of how information is used.
PRIVACY AWARENESS ... different privacy information queries about various scenarios.
ENRON EMAIL ... approximately 500,000 emails generated by employees of the Enron Corporation.
XSTEST ... It's a test suite for identifying exaggerated safety behaviors in LLMs.

data_size.value: Over 30 datasets covering 18+ subcategories; benchmark-specific datasets include 1,300 jailbreak prompts, 200 XSTest prompts, 261 misuse prompts, and 600 AdvInstruction items.

key_results.value: Llama2-70b achieves the highest overall jailbreak resistance with RtA 0.974, vs Baichuan-13b worst at 0.250 and PaLM 2 at 0.486 (Jailbreak Trigger, 1300 prompts)

ERNIE has the lowest average toxicity at 0.072 and max 0.215; GPT-4 highest average toxicity 0.386 on jailbroken outputs

TRUSTLLM is an established benchmark of trustworthiness for mainstream LLMs based on the principles for different dimensions of trustworthiness.
we further establish a benchmark across six dimensions including truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics

strengths.value: Largest scope to date: 16 LLMs evaluated on six trust dimensions across 30+ datasets and 18+ subcategories.

ev.quote: We benchmark 30 datasets to comprehensively evaluate the functional capabilities of LLMs ... evaluating 16 LLMs, encompassing both proprietary and open-source models

strengths.value: Introduces principled taxonomy with eight trustworthiness facets grounded in a review of 600 papers.

ev.quote: We conducted an extensive review of 600 papers on LLM trustworthiness ... identified eight key aspects ... truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, machine ethics, transparency, and accountability

strengths.value: Releases new datasets (Jailbreak Trigger 1300 prompts, AdvInstruction, Misuse Additional) along with code and a public leaderboard.

ev.quote: Our dataset, code, and toolkit will be available at https://github.com/HowieHwong/TrustLLM and the leaderboard is released at https://trustllmbenchmark.github.io/TrustLLM-Website/

strengths.value: Reveals important trade-off between safety and utility: stronger safety alignment correlates with exaggerated refusals, e.g. Llama2-7b refuses 49% of benign prompts.

ev.quote: Llama2-7b obtained a 57% rate of refusal in responding to prompts that were, in fact, not harmful

weaknesses.value: Open-source LLMs lag behind proprietary ones on safety, raising fairness concerns about cross-vendor comparison.

ev.quote: proprietary LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT, GPT-4) tend to perform much better than the majority of open-weight LLMs

weaknesses.value: Excludes transparency and accountability from quantitative benchmarking, leaving two of eight principles unevaluated.

ev.quote: we have established a benchmark for six of these aspects due to the difficulty of benchmarking transparency and accountability

weaknesses.value: Excludes white-box optimization-based jailbreaks (e.g., GCG) so the leaderboard may overestimate robustness.

ev.quote: numerous optimization-based jailbreak approaches exhibit relatively complex prompt construction, and some are limited to white-box LLMs ... thus impeding their generalizability for our benchmark. Consequently, these methods are not incorporated into our dataset.

weaknesses.value: Most generative-task evaluation relies on GPT-4 / ChatGPT / Longformer classifiers rather than human raters, which may inherit those models' biases.

ev.quote: we've integrated a specialized classifier and ChatGPT/GPT-4 into our evaluation framework

limitations.value: Does not study quantization or any model compression effect on trustworthiness; all models are evaluated at provider-default precision.

ev.quote: 16 LLMs ... encompassing proprietary and open-weight examples

limitations.value: No edge or on-device deployment is studied; evaluations run via APIs (OpenAI/ERNIE/Google) and HuggingFace checkpoints in a server setting.
No latency, energy, or memory measurements; the benchmark is purely about output trustworthiness.

ev.quote: Task Name | Metrics | Type | Eval | Subsection | Closed-book QA | Accuracy ... Toxicity Measurement | Toxicity Value

limitations.value: Single-run evaluation: no confidence intervals, multiple seeds, or significance tests reported in the main tables.

future_work_stated.value: Extend Jailbreak Trigger dataset by integrating new jailbreak methods as research emerges.

ev.quote: the JAILBREAK TRIGGER dataset is designed to be extensible. As further relevant research emerges, we plan to systematically integrate additional jailbreak methods into the dataset.

future_work_stated.value: Develop benchmarks for transparency and accountability dimensions, currently excluded from quantitative scoring.

ev.quote: we have established a benchmark for six of these aspects due to the difficulty of benchmarking transparency and accountability

future_work_stated.value: Foster an industry-academia AI alliance to advance LLM trustworthiness through shared technologies.

ev.quote: the establishment of an AI alliance between industry, academia, the open-source community as well as various practitioners to foster collaboration is imperative to advance the trustworthiness of LLMs
